added_lemmas.justification: The bounded-window ancestry condition is exactly the graphical frontier for universal equality with the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast across all admissible positive refinements and models.
added_lemmas.gap: The converse is deliberately contrast-specific: failure permits a full-support model on which the unadjusted contrast is wrong, while a displayed two-lag graph shows that another observed-law adjustment may still identify the causal effect.
added_lemmas.consumer: The collapse theorem uses the forward direction, and analysts use the converse to distinguish maximality of this simple contrast from the stronger and generally false claim of a complete identification criterion.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the exact universal unadjusted-adjustment frontier into the owned collapse theorem and update its node-level positioning without changing the frozen collapse claim.

proposed.justification: The theorem records the singleton sharp-envelope face, while its load-bearing frontier theorem proves that the bounded-window condition is exact for universal equality with the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast.
proposed.gap: This is maximality of one explicit contrast, not a necessary-and-sufficient full-law identification criterion: when the condition fails, an alternative observed adjustment can still identify the effect, as the two-lag counterexample proves.
proposed.consumer: Users obtain the unadjusted contrast and collapsed sharp envelope exactly on its universal graphical regime, while retaining other identification methods when that regime fails.
